newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Endesa up sharply in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Endesa up sharply in thin trade.

text.p: Shares in Spanish electricity firm Endesa were up sharply on Tuesday, outperforming the indices in a session where sellers were thin on the ground, dealers said.
Good prospects for Endesa's autumn privatisation, the payment of a dividend next week and an upcoming share split were all reasons behind the lack of paper, they said.
"At the moment, the way the market is, with very few sellers because of good medium-term (bourse) prospects, any excuse is good enough to send a stock up sharply," said a Madrid dealer.
Some also speculated that after heavier trade yesterday, an entity hoping to become a core investor in Endesa was taking a big position.
But others dismissed this as there was no sign of one clear buyer.
At 1030 GMT Endesa was up 320 pesetas, 2.59 percent, to 12,690 while the Ibex-35 blue chip index was 0.37 percent to 6,909.98.

"Basically what's going on with Endesa is that no-one is selling. We've got the privatisation coming up, and there's a lot of people interested in buying. While that goes on, no one is offering paper," said a trader a foreign brokerage who requested anonymity.
He said these factors, along with a dividend payment on July 7, were likely to continue to give the stock upside.
Volume was around one third of what would be average for Endesa at this time of day, he added.
"The problem now is how are they going to go about the public share offering with the stock nearing 13,000 pesetas. No-one's going to buy it at that level," he said.
State holding company Sepi is due to bring up to 33 percent of the utility's share capital to the market in the autumn, in a placement which is expected to have a large retail tranche.
An analyst at Ahorro Corporacion Financiera said that Monday's heavy trade in Endesa, which saw the shares climb 200 pesetas to 12,370, might be explained by position-taking.

"The only thing that makes sense is that an investor who wants to form part of the core group of shareholders is in there. That's the only type of investor who wouldn't mind buying at these levels. But really there's been no news from Endesa which would justify the recent rise," he said.
Endesa has said it will split its shares four-for-one ahead of the privatisation, although no specific date has yet been announced.
